brief.note: Nothing new cleared 10%; the Toronto market was shut for Thanksgiving and C.H. Robinson aged out.

candidates.name: T-Mobile US, Inc.
candidates.business: Runs the second-largest US mobile network, selling wireless and home broadband
candidates.cause: SpaceX agreed to buy a nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management, setting up Starlink as a direct rival for US mobile customers.
candidates.right: Satellite capacity cannot match dense urban networks and Starlink stays a niche rural rival
candidates.wrong: Starlink wins mainstream subscribers and price competition compresses wireless margins for years

candidates.name: Alignment Healthcare, Inc.
candidates.business: Runs Medicare Advantage health plans for seniors across several US states
candidates.cause: CMS cut the 2027 star rating on its largest California contract to 3.5 from 4.0, costing bonus payments on about 75% of its Medicare Advantage members.

metrics.label: Other plans
metrics.value: Six of seven at 4 stars or better

candidates.right: The contract regains four stars at the next review and the bonus payments return
candidates.wrong: Lost bonus payments squeeze margins for two years while medical costs keep climbing

candidates.name: Webull Corporation
candidates.business: Runs a commission-free share and options trading app for retail investors
candidates.cause: A bipartisan House committee called the broker tied in structural ways to China's government, noting a mainland subsidiary employs about 62% of staff; Webull disputes the findings.
candidates.right: Washington takes no action and the China findings prove political noise rather than a business restriction
candidates.wrong: Regulators force a restructuring, or US brokers and partners quietly step away from Webull
